sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the opening header of the maamar, including the Torah portion and date.

translations.translation: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeira,
20 MarCheshvan 5737

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and the Rebbe's question on the relationship between "the way of Hashem" and "doing charity and justice."

translations.translation: "And Hashem said, 'Shall I conceal from Avraham... and Avraham will surely become a great and mighty nation... For I have known him, so that he will command... and they will keep the way of Hashem, to do charity and justice...'"
And the Baal HaYom Huledes (the Rebbe Rashab) precisely analyzes this in his maamar beginning with these words from the year 5667
(in the continuation of 5666),
[asking:] "The way of Hashem" refers to Torah and mitzvos,
so what does the verse add with "to do charity [etc.]"
(the matter of mitzvos)
beyond "and they will keep the way of Hashem"?
And he explains there,
that "the way of Hashem" is an influence from above downward,
and "charity and justice" is the service in the manner of from below upward,
the service of returning light.
[And based on this, he explains there
also the connection of "and they will keep the way of Hashem, to do charity and justice" to what was stated previously: "And Hashem said, 'Shall I conceal from Avraham...'"]

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contrasts the two maamarim in the series, highlighting their different interpretations of "I have known him" and of "to do charity and justice."

translations.translation: Now, the verse "For I have known him... and they will keep the way of Hashem, to do charity and justice" is explained in the aforementioned continuation in the maamar "Ki Yedativ" of the year 5666
(the first maamar of Shabbos Parshas Vayeira in that continuation),
and in this maamar
(the second maamar of Shabbos Parshas Vayeira in that continuation)
he explains the verse in a different manner.
In addition to the fact that the first maamar begins with the verse "Ki Yedativ" and the second maamar begins with the verse "Vahashem Amar HaMechaseh Ani,"
even regarding the verse "Ki Yedativ" itself,
in the second maamar he explains it differently.
For in the first maamar, he brings two interpretations of "Ki Yedativ":
the interpretation of Targum [Onkelos]
that "Yedativ" is an expression of knowledge,
"for it is revealed before Me,"
and Rashi's interpretation that "Yedativ" is an expression of endearment.
And he explains there
that "Yedativ" as an expression of knowledge refers to the matter of essential will
(for this is "for it is revealed before Me,"
because will is in a state of revelation),
and "Yedativ" as an expression of endearment refers to the matter of essential delight.
However, in the second maamar
he explains
"Yedativ" as an expression of endearment,
that He cherished him in the aspect of essential delight.
And there is another difference between the two maamarim in the interpretation of "and they will keep the way of Hashem, to do charity and justice."
For in the first maamar it implies
(according to the simple meaning of the verse's language,
and as is also explained in several discourses)
that "to do charity and justice" is the explanation of "and they will keep the way of Hashem,"
or that charity and justice is a detail within "the way of Hashem."
And it can be said that "the way of Hashem"
(in the singular)
is the Torah
(the aspect of the general principle that is above division),
and from this flows "to do charity,"
the performance of mitzvos
(the 248 limbs of the King,
particular limbs).
But in this maamar
(the second maamar of Shabbos Parshas Vayeira in that continuation)
he explains that "to do charity [etc.]"
(even though it comes after "and they will keep the way of Hashem")
is not an explanation or a detail of "the way of Hashem," but rather an additional matter.
For after "and they will keep the way of Hashem,"
an influence from above downward,
they then come
to a more elevated service,
"to do charity,"
service from below upward.
